I don’t think that conclusion fits the evidence, but we don’t have to rely on space photos to examine it. Long before satellites existed, people noticed that Earth casts a curved shadow on the Moon during lunar eclipses and that different stars become visible as you travel north or south. You can also estimate Earth’s circumference by comparing shadows at two distant locations at the same time.

Is there a particular observation that convinced you Earth is flat? We could look at what each model predicts and see which prediction matches what we can actually measure.

3

Sunlight looks white, but it’s a mixture of colors. When it enters Earth’s atmosphere, it encounters tiny molecules of nitrogen and oxygen. Those molecules scatter some of the light, sending it off in different directions.

Here’s the important part: they scatter shorter wavelengths much more strongly than longer ones. Blue light has a shorter wavelength than red light, so much more blue gets scattered across the sky and into your eyes—even when you’re looking far away from the Sun.

You might ask: isn’t violet’s wavelength even shorter? Yes! But sunlight contains less violet, and our eyes are much more sensitive to blue.

At sunset, sunlight travels through more atmosphere before reaching you. Much of the blue has been scattered away from that direct path, leaving the reds and oranges that make sunsets glow.

雨下到深夜，街道渐渐空了。路灯把细密的雨丝照成金线，积水里浮着一盏盏摇晃的光。便利店的门开了一下，暖黄的亮色和关东煮的热气一起涌出来，又很快被夜风收走。楼上的窗半掩着，有人伸手接住檐下滴落的水。远处驶来末班公交，轮胎碾过水洼，哗的一声，惊动了蜷在屋檐下的猫。我关掉台灯，听雨点敲着窗沿，忽然觉得，今晚不必急着睡去。
